answer_ordering_note: Canonical answers are unchanged from the approved question design. Only option positions are reordered so the correct position is distributed across A/B/C/D rather than repeated as A.

items.prompt: A student must request an internship-related document from a school office. What should be decided first when planning the formal message?

options.text: Add unrelated personal details.
Determine the recipient and the purpose of the request.
Make the message as long as possible.
Begin with casual language to sound friendly.

items.explanation: The recipient and purpose establish what the message needs to communicate and how it should be framed.

provenance.concept: formal communication planning; recipient and purpose

items.prompt: A student needs a school document before a stated internship deadline. Which formulation makes the request clearest?

options.text: Omit the timing because the office can guess it.
Replace the request with a general statement about internships.
State the needed document and the required time clearly.
Hint at the deadline without stating it.

items.explanation: Important information should be explicit enough for the recipient to act without guessing.

provenance.concept: clarity and completeness of formal communication

items.prompt: A draft request to a school administration office contains a highly casual greeting and slang. What is the most appropriate revision?

options.text: Revise the wording so it matches a formal administrative context.
Remove the purpose of the request instead.
Add more slang to make the message warmer.
Keep the slang because the recipient is a school employee.

items.explanation: Register should fit the relationship, purpose, and institutional context.

items.prompt: A school office asks a student to confirm attendance at a career preparation event. Which reply is most complete?

options.text: Send an emoji without text.
Reply only that the message was read.
Reply with an unrelated question.
Confirm attendance and identify the event being confirmed.

items.explanation: The reply should make its purpose and the information being confirmed clear to the recipient.

items.prompt: A student accepts an invitation from a school administration office. Which response is appropriate?

options.text: Use slang because email is a digital medium.
Use concise, polite language suited to the institutional recipient.
Write as if responding to a close friend.
Use only abbreviations and omit the greeting.

items.explanation: The communication medium does not by itself determine the level of formality; recipient and purpose matter.

items.prompt: A school office needs confirmation that a student will attend a specific event on the stated date. Which response supplies the needed information?

options.text: Leave the response blank and rely on the subject line.
Say only "Thanks."
Confirm attendance and refer clearly to the relevant event/date.
Say only "I understand."

items.explanation: A useful confirmation contains the information needed to resolve the request without another clarification cycle.

provenance.concept: information completeness in an official email response

qa_expectations.note: For six items, this is a controlled balanced distribution with all four positions represented. It is not a permanent production randomization algorithm.
